project.name: Secure Document Vault
project.description: Full-stack secure document storage with encryption at rest and in transit

components.nist-justification: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 approves 2048-bit RSA for security strength of 112 bits until 2030
TLS 1.3 with AES-256-GCM provides 128-bit security strength per NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2
Required secure transport prevents plaintext credential and data exposure
RSA-2048 provides 112-bit security strength, sufficient until 2030 per NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Table 2
components.future-plan: Migrate to RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-384 for post-2030 compliance

components.purpose: TLS server authentication for backend API
components.nist-justification: SHA-256 provides 128-bit collision resistance per NIST FIPS 180-4

components.purpose: TLS server and client authentication for MySQL
components.nist-justification: Client certificate authentication prevents unauthorized database access

components.purpose: Encrypt files at rest in database
components.nist-justification: AES-256 provides 128-bit security strength per NIST SP 800-57 Part 1. GCM mode provides authenticated encryption per NIST SP 800-38D

components.key-storage: Never stored (derived on-demand from password hash)
components.nist-justification: SHA-256 provides 128-bit security strength per NIST FIPS 180-4. Each user has unique KEK derived from their password. Follows key hierarchy best practices
components.security-note: Password change breaks file access without DEK re-encryption (not implemented)
components.limitation: Password compromise exposes all user files

components.salt: Random per-password (16 bytes via argon2 library)
components.justification: Argon2id is winner of Password Hashing Competition and recommended by OWASP. Memory-hard algorithm resists GPU/ASIC attacks

components.purpose: Short-lived JWT access tokens for API authentication
components.nist-justification: HMAC-SHA512 provides 256-bit security strength per NIST FIPS 198-1. Short expiry limits exposure window
components.security-note: Stateless tokens, cannot be revoked before expiry

components.purpose: Long-lived JWT refresh tokens for obtaining new access tokens
components.nist-justification: Database storage enables revocation capability. Longer expiry balanced by revocation mechanism per NIST SP 800-63B

components.purpose: Verify configuration and code file integrity at container startup
components.nist-justification: SHA-256 provides 128-bit collision resistance per NIST FIPS 180-4. Detects unauthorized modifications
components.implementation: Checksums generated during build, verified at container startup
components.security-note: Containers fail to start if integrity check fails

components.purpose: Generate cryptographic keys, IVs, salts, and tokens
components.nist-justification: CSPRNG meets NIST SP 800-90A requirements for random number generation

certificate-renewal.future-improvement: Automated renewal with Let's Encrypt or internal CA

jwt-secret-rotation.recommendation: Rotate quarterly or on suspected compromise
jwt-secret-rotation.impact: All active tokens invalidated on rotation

kek-rotation.process: Re-encrypt all DEKs with new KEK
kek-rotation.recommendation: Rotate annually or on suspected compromise

compliance.nist-sp-800-57: All symmetric keys ≥128-bit security strength, asymmetric keys ≥2048-bit RSA
compliance.nist-sp-800-63b: Password hashing with memory-hard function, multi-factor capability via refresh token revocation

protected-against: Token theft with limited exposure (15-minute access token expiry)
Unauthorized database access (TLS client certificates, authentication)
limitations: KEK stored in environment variable (not HSM)

post-quantum-readiness.note: Symmetric algorithms (AES-256) are quantum-resistant. Asymmetric algorithms (RSA-2048) will require upgrade

production-recommendations: TPM 2.0 for certificate and KEK storage
HSM (Hardware Security Module) for KEK protection and cryptographic operations
Secure Boot to ensure integrity verification authenticity
